pharm: HER2-directed antibody conjugated to a topoisomerase I inhibitor payload (deruxtecan) via a cleavable linker; binds HER2, internalises and releases cytotoxic payload with bystander effect on neighbouring cells
quick: 5.4 mg/kg IV every 3 weeks (breast, NSCLC); 6.4 mg/kg IV every 3 weeks (gastric)
Can cause fetal harm; verify status; effective contraception during and for 7 months after last dose
Do not breastfeed during treatment and for 7 months after last dose
No adjustment in mild-moderate impairment; limited data in severe
No adjustment in mild impairment; monitor in moderate-severe (bilirubin)
ILD symptoms, LVEF, CBC, pregnancy status
summary: Trastuzumab deruxtecan (Enhertu) is a HER2-directed antibody-drug conjugate for HER2-positive and HER2-low metastatic breast cancer, HER2-positive gastric cancer, and HER2-mutant non-small-cell lung cancer. It delivers a topoisomerase I inhibitor payload with activity even in low HER2 expression via a bystander effect. Boxed warnings cover interstitial lung disease/pneumonitis (which can be fatal and requires permanent discontinuation at grade 2+), left ventricular dysfunction, and embryo-fetal toxicity.
indications: Unresectable or metastatic HER2-positive breast cancer after prior anti-HER2 therapy
Unresectable or metastatic HER2-low (IHC 1+ or 2+/ISH-) breast cancer after prior chemotherapy
Locally advanced or metastatic HER2-positive gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma after prior trastuzumab-based therapy
Unresectable or metastatic HER2-mutant non-small-cell lung cancer after prior systemic therapy

dosage.d: 5.4 mg/kg IV every 3 weeks until progression or unacceptable toxicity
dosage.t: 90-min first infusion, then 30 min if tolerated; do NOT substitute for trastuzumab or ado-trastuzumab emtansine
dosage.n: Dose-reduce for ILD grade 1 (hold), neutropenia, febrile neutropenia, LVEF decline
Higher ILD vigilance at this dose

admin: For IV infusion after reconstitution and dilution; do not give IV push or bolus
Do not confuse with trastuzumab or ado-trastuzumab emtansine - verify label (medication-error risk)
First infusion over 90 minutes with observation; subsequent over 30 minutes if prior tolerated
Use antiemetic prophylaxis (moderately-highly emetogenic); infusion-set filter per labeling
moa: The trastuzumab component binds HER2 on tumour cells; the complex is internalised and lysosomal cleavage releases deruxtecan (a topoisomerase I inhibitor), causing DNA damage and apoptosis. Membrane-permeable payload diffuses to neighbouring cells (bystander effect), giving activity in heterogeneous and HER2-low tumours.

relative: Pre-existing interstitial lung disease/pneumonitis (risk of fatal ILD; use only if benefit outweighs risk)
Significant cardiac disease or LVEF below institutional lower limit
monitor: New or worsening cough, dyspnoea, fever (possible ILD - hold and evaluate promptly)

preg: No adequate human data. Based on mechanism, fetal harm is expected. Verify pregnancy status before starting; advise effective contraception during treatment and for the specified period after the last dose. Use in pregnancy only if the potential benefit justifies the potential fetal risk. Females use effective contraception during treatment and for 7 months after the last dose; males with female partners use contraception during and for 4 months after.
lact: No data on presence in human milk. Because of potential serious adverse reactions in the breastfed infant, advise women not to breastfeed during treatment and for the specified period after the last dose.
renal: No dose adjustment in mild or moderate renal impairment (CLcr 30-89). Effect of severe impairment or dialysis is unknown; monitor closely.
hepatic: No adjustment in mild hepatic impairment. Limited data in moderate impairment; avoid or monitor closely in severe impairment and hyperbilirubinaemia (payload hepatic clearance).

major: Strong CYP3A/P-gp modulators affecting payload exposure (limited clinical data; monitor toxicity)
Other cardiotoxic or QT-prolonging agents (additive LVEF/QT risk)
interactions.alcohol: No specific interaction; counsel on concomitant risks.
interactions.diagnostics: No characteristic laboratory test interference; monitor disease-specific markers.

serious: Interstitial lung disease / pneumonitis (boxed; can be fatal)
emergency: New/worsening breathlessness, cough or fever (possible ILD) - hold drug and seek urgent evaluation
Chest pain, breathlessness or oedema (possible cardiac dysfunction) - seek emergency care
Fever with neutropenia - seek urgent care

monitoring: ILD symptoms at every visit; low threshold for high-resolution CT; permanently discontinue for grade 2+ ILD
counsel: Report any new cough, breathing difficulty or fever immediately - lung inflammation can be fatal and needs urgent steroids and stopping the drug
Report swelling, rapid weight gain or breathlessness (heart effects)
Use anti-nausea medicines as prescribed; this drug commonly causes nausea
Avoid pregnancy during treatment and for 7 months after; do not breastfeed
This is not the same as trastuzumab (Herceptin) - confirm the exact medicine at each visit
pk: Tumour response typically assessed at 6-9 weeks
End of infusion (antibody); payload released intracellularly over days
Refrigerate 2-8 C; do not freeze; use reconstituted/diluted solution within labeling time limits
pearls: Active in HER2-low disease through the bystander payload effect - a first for HER2 ADCs
ILD is the signature fatal risk: grade 1 holds drug + steroids; grade 2+ permanently discontinues
Never substitute for trastuzumab or T-DM1 - different doses and toxicities (look-alike/sound-alike risk)
LVEF monitoring mirrors other HER2 agents; hold/discontinue per LVEF thresholds
missed: If a planned dose is missed, give it as soon as possible and adjust the schedule to maintain the planned interval; do not double the dose. Consult the full prescribing information for cycle-delay rules.
overdose: No specific antidote. Overdose is expected to exaggerate known toxicities (myelosuppression, GI effects, infusion reactions). Provide supportive care with close monitoring. Contact Poison Help (1-800-222-1222).
